definition: A thermodynamic quantity $S$, in $\text{J K}^{-1}$, that measures the disorder of the particles in a system; it changes by $\Delta S = \frac{\Delta Q}{T}$ when thermal energy is transferred at constant temperature, and equals $k_\text{B}\ln\Omega$ for a state with $\Omega$ microstates.

One particular arrangement of the particles of a system among all the arrangements that give the same macroscopic state; in an isolated system all microstates are equally likely, and $\Omega$ is the number of them.

The total entropy of an isolated system never decreases; equivalently, thermal energy cannot flow by itself from a colder to a hotter body (Clausius), and no cyclic engine can turn all the thermal energy from one reservoir into work (Kelvin).
A process after which the system and its surroundings cannot both be returned to their initial states; every real process is irreversible and increases the total entropy.
